title: Evaluation, datasets & prompts
summary: Know whether a change made the app better before users find out. The support reply gets a dataset with splits and versions, code checks and LLM judges (checked against known grades before they're trusted), experiments compared example by example to find regressions, agent trajectories checked step by step, tests in pytest, prompts kept as versioned commits with a production tag, and a release gate that promotes a prompt only if nothing got worse. The capstone runs the whole improvement loop: users' thumbs-down become a regression set, a fix is evaluated against production, released by moving a tag, and checked on the live app.
learn: **Datasets, targets, evaluators**: code checks, LLM judges, several scores, categories, summary metrics
**Agent evals**: trajectory match modes, tool arguments, trajectory judges, single-step tests
**Comparing versions**: regressions per example, cost and speed, repetitions, pairwise judges
**Tests in pytest**, **local evaluations**, quality gates and **backtesting** on real traffic
**Prompts as versions**, **gated releases** and rollbacks, **monitoring** and online evaluation
flow:
production (prompt tag) ─→ answers ─→ users 👍/👎 ─→ 👎 → regression set
   candidate prompt (a commit) ─→ evaluate on regressions + smoke ─→ nothing worse? ─→ move the production tag ─→ verify

path.title: Production path: the improvement loop
path.summary: The support reply runs whatever the registry's production tag points to, and every answer carries the prompt version. Thumbs-down answers become a regression set; a fix is a new commit, evaluated against production on that set plus the smoke tests; it's released only if nothing got worse, by moving the tag, and verified on the live app.

steps.title: Registry
steps.explain: routers/support.py pulls support-reply:production at runtime (cached a minute); push makes commits, tag moves pointers.
production: With a LangSmith key the same flow runs on the Prompt Hub: push_prompt, pull_prompt, commit tags.

steps.title: Evaluate
steps.explain: facts and no_promises on every example, a judge where code can't decide, all through langsmith.evaluate on outputs computed beforehand.
production: Check a new judge against known grades before it gates anything.

steps.title: Gate
steps.explain: gate() compares per example: any check the production prompt passed and the candidate fails blocks the release.
production: Run it in CI on every prompt change; the tag moves only from the pipeline.

steps.title: Loop
steps.explain:
The capstone: production answers, users' ratings, a regression set from the 👎, the candidate evaluated, released by a tag move, the complaints asked again.

| Step | Measured on the 12-example support dataset |
|---|---|
| Production prompt v1 | 4 of 12 answers got a 👎 (a fact missing). On "How much is a cold brew?" it made up a price ("$4.50"; the menu says ₹200). |
| Candidate v2 (policy in the prompt) | facts 0.9 vs 0.6 on the regression set + smoke, but **blocked**: s1 lost a fact the production answer had |
| Candidate v3 (v2 + apologise first) | facts 1.0, no promises 1.0, nothing got worse: **released** by moving the `production` tag |
| After release | the live app answered all 4 complaints correctly; 12 of 12 answers now rated 👍 |
| ministral-8b vs 14b | 1.8× faster (p50 1569 vs 2793 ms), same tokens, facts 58% vs 67%: it broke s1. A pairwise judge still preferred the 8b answers 3 of 3 times, so check judges per example before trusting them. |

v2's average went up (0.6 → 0.9) while s1 got worse: only the per-example gate caught it.
production: Keep every regression example: the next release is tested against it too.
